description: Canonical runtime authority for HYDI. Declares exactly one supervisor, one boot authority, and one owner per required service, and classifies every other runtime-capable implementation in the tree. This file is the answer to 'who is allowed to start, own, and stop HYDI services'. It is a DECLARATION; enforcement is Phase 2.
createdBy: Phase 1 — Establish Canonical Authority (HYDI Master Execution Contract)

system-manifest.json.reason: It is read at runtime by src/enforcement/RuntimeEnforcer.js, src/enforcement/module-hook.js, src/audit/SystemAuditor.js, src/audit/PreFlightGate.js and scripts/enforce-build-compliance.js. Editing it changes live enforcement behaviour, which needs its own tested change. It is ~5 months stale (lastUpdated 2026-04-29).
system-manifest.json.reconciliationPhase: deferred — must be a standalone, tested change

boot.config.json.role: Declares WHICH modules the boot authority starts and in what dependency order. This manifest declares WHO is allowed to start them.

CANONICAL.md.role: Repo identity only. scripts/verify-canonical.js checks its existence, not its contents.

ACTIVE_TREE.md.role: Human-readable tree identity. No code reads it.

versionConflict.impact: HYDI cannot currently answer 'what version am I?' (Phase 18 requirement). Resolution deferred to its own change — picking a winner arbitrarily would be a guess.

supervisor.role: PROCESS SUPERVISOR OF RECORD. The only component permitted to supervise long-running HYDI processes across reboots.
supervisor.evidence: pm2 jlist shows all 8 online; cwd=C:\Users\Owner\HYDI-System-v2

bootAuthority.role: SERVICE OWNER OF RECORD. The only component permitted to start, own and stop the modules declared in boot.config.json.

canonicalAuthority.rule: Exactly one supervisor. Exactly one boot authority. Exactly one owner per required service. A process answering on a port is NOT proof of ownership.

heidi-web.entrypoint: next (npm run dev | npm run start)

heidi-mobile-chat.note: The only conforming service. It is conforming precisely because it has never been recovered.

job-executor-poller.note: Enabled 5th boot child. Has no health URL, only livenessMs — liveness is not health.

hydi-orchestrator.note: The Observe->Decide->Act core loop. enabled:false and enableAutoActions:false in boot.config.json. The cognitive loop the contract targets is currently NOT running.

hydi-watchdog.role: Observes service health and invokes RecoveryEngine.
hydi-watchdog.conflict: CRITICAL — it invokes RecoveryEngine, which respawns services DETACHED (shell:true, detached:true, unref()). That severs hydi-boot's ownership. The watchdog is the mechanism producing the ORPHAN state above.

hydi-daemon.role: Cognitive cycle heartbeat — sole writer of cognitive_cycle events.

hydi-protoforge-scout.role: External opportunity scouting (HN/Reddit). NOT a code-gap scout.

competingAuthorities.note: Nothing here is deleted. Each is classified and each needs an explicit disposition before Phase 2 can declare ownership provable.

bootOrchestrators.why: Own port check + dependency wait + spawn + crash monitor. Reads .ports.json instead of boot.config.json — a second, divergent module registry.
bootOrchestrators.hazard: Launches 9 services including the LEGACY heidi-core stack (HEIDI Core :3459, HEIDI Agent :3461) and C:\ProtoForge_Ecosystem\heidi-bridge.py -- a path OUTSIDE this repo. Running it on a live box collides with the supervised tree on 3000/3005/3006.

bootOrchestrators.why: Spawns the same daemon as pm2 hydi-daemon in the foreground; both contend for .heidi-daemon.lock.

bootOrchestrators.reachableVia: none (no npm script, no pm2 entry)
bootOrchestrators.why: Drives src/hydi-v3/HYDIContinuousRuntime. Referenced only by tsconfig.typecheck.json.
Alternate boot path: supabase start then npm run boot.

restartKillAuthorities.note: Canonical recovery, but its detached respawn is what breaks ownership.

restartKillAuthorities.defect: protoforge-core and heidi-web are NOT pm2 apps — they are boot-agent children. This call cannot succeed for them.

restartKillAuthorities.note: Kill by image name — can kill unrelated processes sharing an image name.

restartKillAuthorities.defect: SECOND ORPHAN-MAKER. Stops the module then respawns boot-agent detached, producing the same severed ownership as RecoveryEngine.
restartKillAuthorities.note: Reachable from execution path C (heidi-core), which is itself ungoverned.

scheduledTaskInstallers.note: Installers present but nothing registered. If ever run, install-watchdog.ps1 would duplicate pm2 hydi-watchdog.

heidi-core/.why: Complete parallel stack (own package.json, server.js on 3459, heidi-agent.js on 3461, 3 index-clean variants, own autostart). DEPLOYMENT.md still documents it as pm2 app 'heidi' — that app does not exist in ecosystem.config.js.
heidi-core/.caveat: NOT inert: heidi-core/data/heidi_memory.db is a live authoritative store, and heidi-core/actions/action-executor.js is execution path C.

src/hydi-v3/.why: HYDIContinuousRuntime reachable only via CLI drivers; not supervised.

evolution/.why: Real self-development loop code (self-evolve-cycle, findings-to-goals, goal-executor). Not supervised. REUSE TARGET for Phase 15 — do not rebuild.

workers/.why: WorkerOrchestrator + 20 workers; no npm or pm2 reference.

pao-system/.why: Inert scaffolding — risk.engine.ts is an unweighted float score with no tier mapping; task.router.ts has 6 hardcoded routes.

apps/ursula-frontend/.why: Separate Next.js app; contains a cloud-supabase fallback trap at src/lib/api.ts:416.

observedConformance.oneSupervisor: PASS — pm2 is the only registered supervisor; 0 scheduled tasks
observedConformance.oneBootAuthority: PARTIAL — hydi-boot holds the lease, but npm run start:hydi and npm run heidi:start remain reachable alternate authorities
observedConformance.oneOwnerPerService: FAIL — 2 of 3 required services are orphans
observedConformance.oneLeasePerService: PARTIAL — .recovery-leases/ exists for heidi-web and protoforge-core but does not encode ownership
observedConformance.noUnexplainedOrphan: FAIL — 2 orphans, cause identified (detached recovery respawn)
observedConformance.noCompetingWatchdogOwnership: FAIL -- 5 independent restart/kill authorities (was 4; scripts/restart-module.js added)

phase1Verdict.note: Phase 1 asked for a canonical selection and a classification, not for the conflicts to be resolved. Resolving them is Phase 2.

amendments.reason: Independent second inventory pass corroborated classifications and surfaced two additional verified hazards.
